title: Gator Painters vs. Precision Paint Experts

h1: Gator Painters vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Decks and fences take more sun and rain than any painted wall. This guide covers how North Central Florida homeowners can compare staining bids.

sections.h2: Wood outdoors is a different job
body: Gator Painters is one of the painting and property-service companies North Central Florida homeowners may be comparing. If your project is a deck, fence, pergola, or other exposed wood, the bid deserves its own set of questions. Horizontal deck boards take direct sun and standing water, fence pickets get splashed by sprinklers and soaked by storms, and both expand and shrink every day. A coating that works on a wall may not last a season on a deck.

Rather than compare companies, this guide compares approaches. It explains why product type matters so much on exterior wood, what to check before anyone opens a can, and which questions help you line up staining bids on equal terms. The same questions apply whether you are refreshing a small back porch or a long perimeter fence.

Film-forming coatings sit on top of the wood. On exposed horizontal surfaces they can trap moisture and peel, leaving a patchy deck that has to be stripped before it can be redone. Penetrating stains soak into the wood fibers instead, so as they weather they fade rather than flake, which makes the next maintenance coat much simpler.

For exposed wood, Precision Paint Experts uses penetrating stains from premium lines, named on the estimate. Where we spray, we back-brush so the stain works into the grain and the gaps between boards instead of sitting on the surface. Our deck and fence staining page covers the full process, and our wood staining and finishing service handles other exterior wood.

sections.h2: Checking the wood before you stain
body: Stain will not fix soft or rotting boards. Before you collect bids, walk the deck and press on boards near the house, around posts, and at stair stringers. Our article on signs of deck wood rot shows what to look for, and our post on treating a sun-damaged fence covers gray, weathered pickets.
During our walkthrough, the crew lead photographs conditions and takes moisture readings where wood looks suspect, so damaged areas are noted on the estimate rather than discovered halfway through.

sections.h2: Deck and fence questions for every bidder
bullets: What product will be used, and is it a penetrating stain or a film-forming coating?
How will the wood be cleaned and prepared?
Are railings, stairs, and the underside of handrails included?
Will damaged boards be flagged and priced separately?
How many coats, and how is the stain worked into the grain?

The best exterior season here runs from October through May, which suits staining well. Summer work is possible earlier in the day, with attention to dew point and radar. Our free estimate lists surfaces included and excluded, prep, product, and coats, and usually arrives within one business day of the walkthrough.

Leave room for weather in your plans. Wood needs to be dry before stain goes on, so a few days of rain can push a start date. Ask every bidder how they decide the wood is ready, and get that standard in writing.

faqs.q: Is stain or paint better for a Florida deck?
faqs.a: For exposed wood, we use penetrating stains, which soak in and fade rather than peel, making future maintenance simpler.

faqs.q: Do you replace rotten deck boards?
faqs.a: Damaged wood is noted during the walkthrough and listed on the estimate so you can decide on repairs before staining.

faqs.q: Is Precision Paint Experts connected to Gator Painters?
faqs.a: No. We are a separate, locally owned company. This page is a general guide to comparing staining bids.
